title: Two pointers
objective: Solve pair problems in a sorted array with one pass, moving a pointer from each end.

sources.title: Laaksonen, Competitive Programmer's Handbook: the two pointers method

simplifies: This version finds one pair and assumes the array is already sorted. Sorting first costs O(n log n), more than the pointer pass itself.

quiz.prompt: Why must the array be sorted for this to work?

options.text: So moving lo right always makes the sum bigger, and moving hi left makes it smaller
options.explanation: Right. That certainty is what lets each step rule out a whole row of pairs.
It is about correctness: unsorted, moving a pointer could make the sum go either way.
Python does not care; the method does.

quiz.prompt: At most how many steps does it take for n items?

options.explanation: Right. Each step moves one pointer inward, and they meet after at most n − 1 steps.
That is checking every pair. Two pointers avoid it.
It does not halve anything; each step moves one pointer by one.
